title: runtime: classify KV/prefix cache outcome (hit/miss/partial) and emit structured cache event
author: Samir Qureshi
release_notes: Runtime now emits a structured `kv_cache_event_v2` payload including per-request cache outcome classification (HIT/MISS/PARTIAL) plus token/byte accounting for dashboards and Optimize hit-rate recommendations (behind `runtime.cache_telemetry_v2`).
description:
Context: As part of ENG-4814 (cache hit-rate instrumentation sprint), we need a consistent per-request cache outcome signal and a structured event payload that downstream aggregation can trust. Prior PRs (PR-18421, PR-18436) added low-level lookup/insert counters + saved_prefill_ms estimation. This PR adds a deterministic outcome classifier (hit/miss/partial) and emits a single structured event per request to the telemetry sink (behind a feature flag) to unblock dashboards/alerts and Optimize recommendations.

What’s in this PR: 1) Outcome classification: Adds `CacheOutcome` enum {HIT, MISS, PARTIAL} computed at end-of-prefill for each request. The classifier uses cached-prefill token counts: HIT = cached_prefill_tokens == requested_prefill_tokens (and requested_prefill_tokens > 0); MISS = cached_prefill_tokens == 0; PARTIAL = 0 < cached_prefill_tokens < requested_prefill_tokens. Requests with no prefill (e.g., decode-only continuation) are emitted with outcome=MISS and `requested_prefill_tokens=0` (explicit field) so they can be filtered downstream. 2) Structured event payload: Emits `kv_cache_event_v2` once per request with stable, low-cardinality fields (no raw request_id, no raw prefix). Includes: outcome, requested_prefill_tokens, cached_prefill_tokens, hit_bytes_estimate, lookup_count, insert_count, evict_count (if available), saved_prefill_ms_estimate, model_runtime_id, cache_namespace, and `prefix_bucket` (64-bit hash bucket) for coarse clustering. 3) Sampling + overhead: Event emission is gated behind `runtime.cache_telemetry_v2` and uses the existing per-tenant sampling config hook; default sampling is 1.0 for canary, 0.05 for general tiers (configurable). Hot-path work is constant-time and avoids allocations by using a small stack struct and deferred serialization. 4) Tests/validation: Adds synthetic cache fixtures for full hit, miss, and partial-prefill cases, plus a fuzz-ish test for edge cases where cached tokens exceed requested tokens due to truncated input normalization (we clamp and record `classifier_clamped=true`).

Non-goals / follow-ups: - No changes to cache algorithm or eviction policy. - Gateway/control-plane attribution tags (route/model/version/region/tenant) are not attached here; that’s handled in the platform PR (PR-18461). - Known limitation: retried streaming requests may produce multiple events; we include `attempt_index` and `is_retry` fields to support dedupe/filters downstream.

Metrics impact: Microbench in `runtime/perf/cache_telemetry` shows +0.3% CPU at p95 and no measurable GPU impact at steady-state on A100/H100 for the cache-heavy scenario. Full perf-canary gating is tracked in ENG-4819.

Rollout: Behind `runtime.cache_telemetry_v2` (off by default). Safe to ship to main; enablement via staged flags by region/tier as per the rollout plan.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for HIT/MISS/PARTIAL classification - [x] Serialization tests for event payload schema - [x] Benchmarks for overhead (CPU/GPU) - [x] Docs/comments for field semantics and clamping behavior - [x] Backwards compatible with older sinks (event name is new)

Example event (redacted): `kv_cache_event_v2 outcome=PARTIAL requested_prefill_tokens=1536 cached_prefill_tokens=1024 hit_bytes_estimate=4194304 saved_prefill_ms_estimate=7.8 prefix_bucket=0x12b4a9c33a4f... cache_namespace=default model_runtime_id=llama-3-70b-q4 attempt_index=0 is_retry=false`
commits: runtime/cache: add CacheOutcome enum + classifier based on cached/requested prefill tokens
runtime/telemetry: introduce kv_cache_event_v2 payload + sink emitter (flagged)
runtime/cache: track requested_prefill_tokens + cached_prefill_tokens in request context
tests: add fixtures for hit/miss/partial-prefill and clamp edge cases
perf: wire cache telemetry bench to validate allocation-free emission
ci_summary: Checks: build (linux-x86_64) ✅; unit-tests (runtime) ✅; clang-tidy ✅; sanitizer (asan/ubsan) ✅; perf-smoke (cache_telemetry) ✅; format ✅
conversation:
Omar El-Sayed (review): The classifier logic looks fine, but I’m worried about the `cached >= requested => HIT` path hiding weird accounting bugs. Can we clamp + explicitly mark when cached > requested? Also please confirm we aren’t allocating on the hot path when emitting the event.

Samir Qureshi (author): Good call. I added `classifier_clamped` and clamp cached_prefill_tokens to requested_prefill_tokens for the emitted event, while still keeping the raw counters in debug logs. Added a unit test that reproduces the cached>requested case via truncated normalization. Also confirmed emission uses stack struct + deferred encoding; no heap allocs unless the sink is enabled and sampling passes.

Noah Patel (review): Can you clarify semantics for decode-only requests? If requested_prefill_tokens=0, outcome=MISS seems okay, but dashboards might interpret as miss. Would rather downstream filter those out.

Samir Qureshi (author): Agree. Included explicit `requested_prefill_tokens` field and documented that hit-rate dashboards should filter requested_prefill_tokens>0. We also tag `prefill_present` in the payload doc (as derived condition) but didn’t add another boolean to keep payload minimal.

Logan Wright (review): Please ensure field names match the v2 spec draft: `saved_prefill_ms_estimate` (not `saved_prefill_ms`) and `prefix_bucket` must be a bounded bucket (not raw hash) to avoid accidental high cardinality in traces. Also, do not include request_id.

Samir Qureshi (author): Updated to `saved_prefill_ms_estimate` and switched `prefix_bucket` to a 64-bit bucketing function (hash then fold to configured bucket count) with default 4096 buckets; bucket count is configurable via flag for canary experiments. No request_id is included.

Nadia Rahman (review): One more: event emission should be at end-of-prefill. If we emit earlier, partial-prefill could flip later in the request lifecycle. Also add `attempt_index/is_retry` for retries so we can dedupe in pipeline.

Samir Qureshi (author): Emission now happens at prefill completion (after cache lookup/insert has settled). Added `attempt_index` and `is_retry` sourced from the existing request context.

Marcus Reed (review): Perf numbers look good, but can we include the benchmark command + acceptance threshold in the PR description for future regressions?

Samir Qureshi (author): Added the bench command and noted overhead target (<1% CPU p95). Also attached the latest run from A100/H100 in the perf-smoke output.

Allison Grant (comment-only): Thanks for avoiding request_id; please keep event schema stable since dashboards will depend on it.

Omar El-Sayed (final review): LGTM after clamp + retry fields. Please squash.

Merge: Squash merge by Samir Qureshi after all required checks passed and approvals received.
merge_outcome: Merged into main as 1 commit: `runtime: emit kv_cache_event_v2 with cache outcome classification`
